summary: A Bitcraze forum thread in the Developer discussions board where user aesreal asks whether a built-in ROS terminal tool exists to set Crazyflie parameters, noting that listParams is the closest existing tool and that his self-written setParam program compiled but did not work. Maintainer whoenig replies that such a tool would be a useful addition, explains that crazyflie_tools use point-to-point communication so parallel parameter changes are not yet possible, and says crazyflie_cpp can establish a connection in under one second. The user then opens an issue in the crazyflie_ros repository.
one_line: Forum thread on setting Crazyflie parameters from a ROS terminal command, with maintainer replies on crazyflie_cpp versus the Python client.
key_facts: The thread is titled 'Setting parameters via terminal [ROS]' and is filed under Firmware/software/electronics on the Bitcraze Forums.
User aesreal posted the original question on Thu Jun 14, 2018 at 4:49 am.
aesreal wanted a command such as rosrun crazyflie_tools setParam to change Crazyflie parameters from the terminal, because he uses more than one Crazyflie.
aesreal said he had searched crazyflie_tools and the closest existing executable was listParams.
aesreal said his self-written setParam executable compiled but did not work, and that he did not know C++ at all.
aesreal's setParam.cpp was based on listParams.cpp from whoenig's crazyflie_ros and used boost::program_options with options uri, param and value.
aesreal said crazyflie.open_link(uri) in the Python client takes more than 2 seconds and establishes a blocking connection.
whoenig replied on Thu Jun 14, 2018 that a parameter-setting tool would be a great addition and suggested opening an issue in the crazyflie_tools repository.
whoenig stated that all crazyflie_tools use point-to-point communication, so changing parameters in parallel is not possible yet.
whoenig stated that the crazyswarm project runs crazyflie_tools in a loop for each Crazyflie, and that parameter changes via broadcast are not yet implemented.
whoenig stated that crazyflie_cpp has no connection concept like the Python client, but individual commands may fail on timeout.
whoenig stated that crazyflie_cpp can establish a connection in under 1 second.

aesreal replied on Fri Jun 15, 2018 that he was extending chooser.py to control LED rings and wanted to add parameter changes, and that he opened an issue at github.com/whoenig/crazyflie_ros/issues/98.
aesreal concluded that cfclient suits stability, flight statistics and configuration, while crazyflie_cpp suits controlling multiple drones with faster communication.
